title: Divergence detection — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #156 (backend-divergence-detection), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: app/signals/divergence.py's `_evaluate_pair` calls `is_beyond_reference_line(...)` for RSI (indicator_name == "rsi") without explicitly passing `oversold=_RSI_OVERSOLD, overbought=_RSI_OVERBOUGHT` -- it silently falls back to the function's own default parameters, which are `_STOCHASTIC_OVERSOLD`/`_STOCHASTIC_OVERBOUGHT`. Correct today only because `_RSI_OVERSOLD == _STOCHASTIC_OVERSOLD == 30.0` and `_RSI_OVERBOUGHT == _STOCHASTIC_OVERBOUGHT == 70.0` -- but the two constant pairs were deliberately kept distinct (per this task's own `decisions` entry) specifically so RSI's reference line could diverge from Stochastic's later. If either pair is ever changed independently without also fixing this call site, `Divergence.beyond_reference_line` would silently compute RSI divergences against the wrong (Stochastic's) thresholds, and no existing test would catch the drift (every fixture uses 30/70 for both). Pass the RSI constants explicitly for indicator_name == "rsi".

`confirmed_divergence_as_of`'s no-look-ahead guarantee has a narrow leak for a swing point born from a run of 3+ exact-value-tied consecutive bars (app/signals/swing_points.py's `_merge_plateau_runs` middle-bar convention). Demonstrated concretely: for `vals=[10,9,8,7,6,5,5,5,5,5,6,7,8,9,10,...]` (a 5-bar plateau at indices 5-9), `swing_lows(series, window=3)` over the FULL series reports the merged point at index 7; the cache's own confirm threshold for that point is `7 + window(3) = 10`, but `swing_lows` on the series truncated to position 10 (i.e. the data a genuinely causal per-bar recomputation would have) still reports index 6, not 7 -- convergence to index 7 only happens once truncated at position 11. So at position 10, `confirmed_divergence_as_of` reports a swing point one bar earlier than a truly causal recomputation would, a real (if narrow) look-ahead leak. Requires an exact multi-bar tie in real float price/indicator data, which is vanishingly rare outside synthetic data (same reasoning backend-divergence-detection's own decisions entry already applies to the spacing-filter question) -- but that decisions entry's 'no mitigation needed' conclusion only analyzed spacing-filter distortion, not this separate confirm-threshold correctness question, so it wasn't actually covered. Worth either tightening the confirm-threshold check to use the plateau run's own last raw-candidate position (not just the merged point's reported position), or explicitly documenting this residual gap next to that decisions entry.
